title: Show the machine's work envelope in the viewport (Browser checkbox)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "in the browser tab add checkbox.. That IF a machine is selected, makes "box" showing the machines work envelope.. if its a cylinder, box, whatever. In the end, the fixture and model "sits" on the floor of the envelope, lathes sits on the end of "cylinder".. work it out."

What is missing: a mounted machine's travel limits are used by the checks, but the viewport never shows them, so the user cannot see whether the part and its fixtures fit the machine.

Wanted:
- A checkbox in the Browser panel ("Show work envelope"), enabled only when the active setup has a machine (its own or the document's). Off by default. It is view state, like the setup eye of issue 1494: not undoable, no command, and it never changes what generates or posts.
- When on, the viewport draws the machine's work envelope as a thin outline with faint faces, from the machine definition already loaded (axis travels; no new figures invented):
  - a milling machine: the box of its X/Y/Z travel;
  - a lathe: a cylinder of its swing and its Z travel, on the spindle axis;
  - a machine with rotary axes: the linear-travel box (the rotary reach is not drawn in the first slice).
- Placement: the envelope is drawn where the machine puts it relative to the setup. Mill: the envelope's floor is the table top, and the fixtures and the model sit on that floor (the fixture stack and table position the setup already knows). Lathe: the chuck face is the end of the cylinder, and the part sits on it, along the spindle axis.
- A machine whose definition lacks the figures needed (no travels, no table position) draws nothing and the checkbox says why in its tooltip; no guessed envelope.

Open points for the worker to settle and record in `docs/decisions/`: where the envelope sits when the setup has no fixture or table position stated (suggested: floor at the lowest point of stock and fixtures, centred in XY, and labelled as "not placed"); whether the envelope is the tool-tip travel or the table-relative volume (state which in the tooltip).

Safety: display only. The envelope must come from the same machine figures the travel and collision checks read, so the picture cannot disagree with a refusal. Nothing here loosens or replaces a check.

Done means: with a mill mounted, ticking the box shows the travel box with the model and fixture standing on its floor; with a lathe, a cylinder with the part on its chuck end; with no machine the checkbox is disabled; a machine without travel figures shows the reason; the structural ui test covers the checkbox states and that toggling it changes no command history and no posted output.
